subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: Should plugin text transforms continue to apply to tool-call argument strings by default, and if so what path-aware or owner-declared boundary should prevent filesystem path misrouting?
rationale: Current main intentionally supports output transforms in tool-call arguments for privacy/masking plugins, but this issue shows that the same behavior can silently redirect file operations; choosing the durable boundary affects public plugin/provider/CLI semantics.

options.title: Path-aware transform boundary
options.body: Keep tool-call argument transforms enabled, but skip or constrain replacements in filesystem-path contexts with tests and clear docs for plugin authors.

options.title: Owner-declared transform scopes
options.body: Require plugin/backend transforms to declare whether they apply to conversational text, tool arguments, or persistence surfaces, avoiding heuristic path detection at the cost of a larger API change.

options.title: Disable argument transforms by default
options.body: Stop applying text transforms to tool-call arguments unless explicitly opted in, reducing path risk but potentially regressing current masking/privacy plugin behavior fixed by the recent merged change.

recommendation.title: Path-aware transform boundary
recommendation.body: Keep tool-call argument transforms enabled, but skip or constrain replacements in filesystem-path contexts with tests and clear docs for plugin authors.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the transform surface and has the strongest history signal for deciding the plugin/runtime compatibility boundary.
